rv.q: It's quite an eloquent study of the dreams that these young men conjure and what they might be willing to do to make them come true.
Pass Over successfully strikes a balance between hope and despair, as the audience watches the two characters dream out loud, turning the stage into a playground of possibility.

FJT artistic director Tim Rhoze's direction keeps the dialogue between the two men humming, and the balance between Meekie's slightly more choleric Moses and Norwood's playful Kitch makes for many charming moments.
Vicious and unnerving, “Pass Over” captures the spirit of the times.
This illuminating and powerful story about the lives and dreams of two black men is both profound and enlightening.

cn.t: This powerful revival of Nwandu's provocative play about Black male bonding and police violence feels timely and illuminating, driven by searing performances and skillful direction that balances profound social commentary with moments of humor.
